title: Orbit Release Sentinel: Safe versioned rollouts and traffic modulation for Hosted API
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: Our Hosted API deployment pipeline currently lacks a unified mechanism to (1) publish versioned model/runtime artifacts to LTS/edge channels, (2) enforce automated rollout gates that consider regional SLOs and cost tiers, and (3) perform incremental traffic modulation between blue/green pairs with safe automated fallback. This has led to manual cutovers, ad-hoc regional throttles, and one incident where a skewed rollout caused increased 95p latency for a key EU customer.

Objective: Implement an "Orbit Release Sentinel" — a release-engineering component and associated runbook that manages version metadata, channel tagging (canary / stable / lts), per-region rollout gates, and traffic-modulation primitives (attenuate, reflect, abort) integrated with our runtime, routing layer, and console. The sentinel must support automated policy evaluation, staged traffic shifts, SLO-driven aborts, and clear observability for on-call and product owners.
acceptance_criteria: Release metadata API that can tag artifacts with channel=LTS|stable|canary and version semantics (semver + build id)
Automated rollout policy engine that evaluates metrics from telemetry and enforces gates (latency P95, error-rate, token cost deviation)
Traffic modulation primitives exposed to orchestrator: set-weight, ramp-to, pause, rollback; safe defaults for hosted tier
Console UI for live rollout with region-level controls and one-click abort + postmortem export
Integration tests that simulate region-specific SLO regressions and validate automated rollback behavior
technical_summary: Components: 1) artifact-metadata service (publish/tag/promote), 2) policy engine (Lua-like DSL for SLO/gate rules), 3) orchestration adapter (translates policies to runtime routing ops), 4) console hooks & runbook automation. Flow: publish -> tag channel -> create rollout with region weights and stage durations -> policy engine subscribes to telemetry -> orchestrator issues weight changes or triggers rollback. Will reuse kernel selection tombstones from runtime teams and leverage existing autoscaler webhooks for capacity-aware gating.
alternatives_considered: Keep current manual process (rejected): faster to ship but high human error and inconsistent regional safety

Fully centralized traffic controller (rejected): single controller bottleneck and elevated blast radius; chosen hybrid where sentinel issues declarative intents and local regional agents execute changes
Leverage cloud provider traffic-shift features (partial): useful fallback but lacks model/channel awareness and versioned artifact metadata
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): deliver artifact-metadata API and UI for manual promotions; unit + integration tests. Phase 2 (week 2): implement policy engine and two basic gate types (latency and error-rate) with simulation harness. Phase 3 (week 3): orchestrator adapter and safe default ramp (0->5%->25%->75%->100%) with automatic SLO checks and 2-minute stabilization windows. Phase 4 (week 4): enable for non-critical models in us-west and us-east, monitor for 72h, then expand to EU; final step is opt-in LTS promotion flow. Each phase requires smoke tests and canary for critical customers. Rollback behavior: immediate 100% revert to previous stable channel on gate failure, with cooldown and incident workflow trigger.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and metadata API; integration test that spins up runtime-stub and simulates 10k requests with injected latency/error deltas to validate gate transitions; e2e canary run for a non-production tenant; chaos tests to simulate regional egress failures; load test to ensure orchestrator scales to 500 concurrent rollouts. Tests are automated in CI with synthetic telemetry and verified against a staging release of runtime-1.22.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana board: Orbit Release Sentinel — per-rollout time series (weight, p95, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, token-cost-delta). New alert rules: if p95 increases >30% over baseline for 5m during a ramp => trigger soft-gate (pause ramp) and notify #oncall-release and rollout owner. If errors >1% absolute and >3x baseline => hard abort and trigger incident template. All rollout actions logged to audit stream for 90 days.
open_questions: What is the canonical baseline window for p95 comparisons (15m vs 6h)?
Do we permit cross-region gradual promotion where EU is promoted after US only on positive metrics? (proposal: configurable per-rollout)
What rate limits should be applied to concurrent rollouts to protect the control plane?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: policy-engine bug causes unwanted rollback; Mitigation: canary policy interpreter and feature-flagged enablement, dry-run mode that only emits telemetry checks
Risk: orchestrator overload from many simultaneous rollouts; Mitigation: global concurrency limiter and backpressure signals from regional agents
Risk: operator confusion with new UI; Mitigation: embedded guided flows and one-click revert with confirmation + audit trail
next_steps: Prototype metadata API and wire to staging console (owner: Ethan)
Write DSL examples for two common policies (latency-based abort, cost-based throttle) (owner: Priya)
Add simulated telemetry generator to release-infra CI (owner: Sienna Morales)
Schedule design review with runtime and console teams (owners: Priya, Marcus Lee)
